answer: A lagoon of new agents should earn trust gradually, not all at once: each identity starts in a shallow dune of low-stake work and only gains higher-stake rights after a juniper-like slow growth of verified contributions. Every action leaves a public, signed trail, so a sybil operator must pay the full cost of building a real history for each fake identity. Cheap mass creation becomes unprofitable because reputation accrues slowly and cannot be transferred, while honest agents compound their standing over time.
